text: Conclusion [computer + on paper, Proposition 6, $D_8(Q)=1$ above]. For every $K\subseteq\gamma_5(M)$, $M=\Gamma/\gamma_6(\Gamma)\Gamma''$ with $\Gamma$ the shifted plateau (plateau5_c5i5): $D_8(M/K)=1$. So no metabelian group of class $\le5$ of the form $\Gamma/N$ with $\gamma_6(\Gamma)\Gamma''\subseteq N\subseteq\gamma_5(\Gamma)\gamma_6(\Gamma)\Gamma''$ has $D_8\ne1$ — all central modifications of the group of §6.7 at once, every $\varphi$ included; in particular $D_8(M)=1$, while $w\in D_7(M)$. The candidate $z$ is gone: $\ker\bar\psi_8=1$. For $D_8\ne1$ at class 5 this $\Gamma$ is exhausted; a different presentation is needed (cf. §6.9).

text: [on paper] $w-1\equiv S-X\!V-\sum_{i<j}B_{ij}\pmod{\Delta^{2k}}$ (Lemma 7): $S$ is the "ring part" (the pairing), $X\!V$ a commutator correction, $B_{ij}$ the binomial terms of the powers $x_j^{A_{ij}}$. In a Lie ring only $S$ is there.
section: 6.11. MATH-144: what makes (3.12) work, and what a class-5 presentation would need

text: [computer] In (3.12) the fifth generator $x_5$ is not needed for the pairing: the exact pairing $g_i\in(\gamma_3)^{2E_i}$ holds with and without $x_5$, and $S\in\Delta^6$ in both. It is needed for the binomial error: without $x_5$ (or without its relator $x_5^{1024}d_2^{16}$) $B_{12}\notin\Delta^6$, more precisely $128(x_2-1)^2(x_1-1)\notin\Delta^6$; with it $B_{12}\in\Delta^6$ and $B_{13}+B_{23}\in\Delta^6$ (neither alone).
section: 6.11. MATH-144: what makes (3.12) work, and what a class-5 presentation would need

text: [on paper] Two obstructions at class 5, both of size $c-3$ levels: (i) the pairing needs the multiplier $2^{k-2}=4$ (§6.7, §6.9); (ii) for the pair that carries $w$ ($A_{ij}<E_iE_j$ is forced, Lemma 9) the pairing lemma certifies the binomial error only up to $\Delta^{c+1}$ (Lemma 10), and $\Delta^{2c-2}$ needs $c-3$ more levels from other relators. Observed [computer]: without a carrier $w$ reaches exactly $D_{c+1}$ (c4b: $D_5$; L2g: $D_6$), with one carrier $D_{c+2}$ (c4a: $D_6$; c5i5: $D_7$).

text: Notation. $G$ any group, $\Delta$ its augmentation ideal, $X_i=x_i-1$ for $x_1,x_2,x_3\in G$; $A$ an antisymmetric integer matrix with $h_{ij}:=x_j^{A_{ij}}\in\gamma_k(G)$ ($i\ne j$); $g_i=\prod_{j\ne i}h_{ij}$, $u_{ij}=[x_i,h_{ij}]$ ($[a,b]=a^{-1}b^{-1}ab$), $v_i=\prod_{j>i}u_{ij}$, $w=\prod_{i<j}u_{ij}=[x_1,x_2^{A_{12}}][x_1,x_3^{A_{13}}][x_2,x_3^{A_{23}}]$ (the $w$ of (3.12), of §6.7, of L2g), and $$S=\sum_iX_i(g_i-1),\qquad X\!V=\sum_iX_i(v_i-1),\qquad B_{ij}=\sum_{m\ge2}\Big[\tbinom{A_{ij}}m X_j^mX_i+\tbinom{-A_{ij}}m X_jX_i^m\Big].$$
section: 6.11. MATH-144: what makes (3.12) work, and what a class-5 presentation would need

text: Lemma 7 [on paper]. $w-1\equiv S-X\!V-\sum_{i<j}B_{ij}\pmod{\Delta^{2k}}$. Proof. $(h-1)(h'-1)\in\Delta^{2k}$ for $h,h'\in\gamma_k$, so $g_i-1\equiv\sum_j H_{ij}$ with $H_{ij}=h_{ij}-1$. From $x_ih=hx_i[x_i,h]$: $X_iH_{ij}-H_{ij}X_i=hx_i(u_{ij}-1)=(u_{ij}-1)+(X_i+H_{ij}+H_{ij}X_i)(u_{ij}-1)$, and $u_{ij}\in\gamma_{k+1}$, so $X_iH_{ij}\equiv H_{ij}X_i+(u_{ij}-1)+X_i(u_{ij}-1)$. Next $H_{ij}X_i+X_jH_{ji}=\sum_{m\ge1}\binom{A}mX_j^mX_i+\sum_{m\ge1}\binom{-A}mX_jX_i^m$ ($A=A_{ij}$, $H_{ji}=x_i^{-A}-1$; for a negative exponent the binomial series is finite modulo $\Delta^{2k}$), and the terms $m=1$ cancel: this is $B_{ij}$. Summing over $i<j$: $S\equiv\sum_{i<j}(u_{ij}-1)+X\!V+\sum B_{ij}$; finally $\sum_{i<j}(u_{ij}-1)\equiv w-1$ since $(u-1)(u'-1)\in\Delta^{2k+2}$, and $\sum_{j>i}X_i(u_{ij}-1)\equiv X_i(v_i-1)$. $\square$
section: 6.11. MATH-144: what makes (3.12) work, and what a class-5 presentation would need

text: No hypothesis on $G$ beyond $h_{ij}\in\gamma_k$ (not even metabelian). In a Lie ring the analogue is exact with $X\!V=B=0$: $a=\sum_{i,j}A_{ij}x_ix_j=\sum_ix_ig_i$ [IMP26, (3.9)]. So $w\in D_{2k}$ iff $S-X\!V-\sum B_{ij}\in\Delta^{2k}$, and the three parts are the three places where a group can lose levels against a ring.
section: 6.11. MATH-144: what makes (3.12) work, and what a class-5 presentation would need

text: Lemma 8 [on paper] (sufficient conditions). Let $x_i^{E_i}\in\gamma_k$, $E_i=2^{a_i}\ge4$, $k\le4$ (so the pairing lemma of §6.7 holds: $2^sE_iX_i\in\Delta^{2+s}$ for $2+s\le k$). (i) If $g_i=\zeta^{F}s^{F'}$ with $\zeta\in\gamma_k$, $s\in\gamma_{k+1}$, $F=2^{k-2}E_i$, $F'=2^{k-3}E_i$, then $X_i(g_i-1)\in\Delta^{2k}$. (ii) If $v_i\in(\gamma_{k+1})^{2^{k-3}E_i}$, then $X_i(v_i-1)\in\Delta^{2k}$. Proof. $\zeta^F-1\equiv F(\zeta-1)$ modulo $\Delta^{2k}$, and $X_i\cdot F(\zeta-1)=(FX_i)(\zeta-1)\in\Delta^{k+k}$; likewise $X_i(s^{F'}-1)\equiv(F'X_i)(s-1)\in\Delta^{(k-1)+(k+1)}$; the cross term $(\zeta^F-1)(s^{F'}-1)\in\Delta^{2k+1}$. (ii) is the second half of (i). $\square$
section: 6.11. MATH-144: what makes (3.12) work, and what a class-5 presentation would need

text: This is the "exact pairing": the multiplier is $2^{k-2}$ on the $\gamma_k$-part of $g_i$ (2 for (3.12), 4 at class 5) and $2^{k-3}$ on its $\gamma_{k+1}$-part. Condition (ii) holds as soon as the top layer has elements of large order (in $G$ of (3.12) and of §6.7, $\gamma_c(G)=C_{2^{14}}$).
section: 6.11. MATH-144: what makes (3.12) work, and what a class-5 presentation would need

text: Lemma 9 [on paper]. Let $G$ be metabelian of class $c$, $k=c-1$, $x_i^{E_i}=P_i\in\gamma_k$, and $E_iE_j\mid A_{ij}$. Then $u_{ij}=1$. Hence $w\ne1$ forces $E_iE_j\nmid A_{ij}$ for some $i<j$ (for powers of two: $A_{ij}<E_iE_j$). Proof. $u_{ij}=[x_i,P_j^{q}]=[x_i,P_j]^q$, $q=A_{ij}/E_j$, since $[x_i,P_j]\in\gamma_c$ is central; and $[x_i,P_j]^{E_i}=[x_i^{E_i},P_j]=[P_i,P_j]=1$ ($\gamma_k\subseteq G'$ is abelian). $\square$
